source: Yunlin County Year 115 curriculum (uploaded by user)
note: Topic/subtopic fields are Pawn to Professor editorial classifications; objective/vocabulary/target language are curriculum-derived.

units.title: Greeting
units.objective: Students can confidently introduce themselves and ask for others' names using basic greetings.

units.title: How Old Am I?
units.objective: Students can accurately use numbers 1–10 to express age, quantity, and personal contact info. Recognize numerals (1–10) first; high-level classes can attempt the written words (one–ten).

units.title: My Family, My Pet and Me
units.objective: Students can identify and introduce their family members and pets using target sentence patterns.

units.title: Beautiful Color, My Feelings
units.objective: Students can connect colors with emotions and ask / answer questions about feelings.

units.title: Festivals and Holidays
units.objective: Students can distinguish between different New Year traditions and express festive wishes in English.

units.title: I Am a Star
units.objective: Students can use "can" to interview peers, record data, and express individual abilities.

units.title: Getting To Know My Class
units.objective: Students can identify common classroom objects and ask/answer questions about ownership.

units.title: Our School
units.objective: Students can identify school staff roles and briefly describe people within the school community.

units.title: My Campus Life
units.objective: Students can describe common school activities and recognize proper sentence structures.

units.title: My Favorite Campus Corner (1)
units.objective: Students can identify key school locations and state their personal preferences.

units.title: My Favorite Campus Corner (2)
units.objective: Students can associate school locations with activities and express them in complete sentences.
target: I can play at the playground.

units.title: Flexibility — Holidays
units.objective: Students can use key holiday vocabulary in meaningful social contexts and experience cultural traditions.

units.title: My Community
units.objective: Students can visually identify and name 10 essential community locations and verbally state their own location using the formula "I am at the..." when prompted with heavy visual support.

units.title: My Community Life
units.objective: Students can recognize simple digital and analog clock times (focusing on hours and basic intervals) and link a specific time to a community location.
target: I go to the park at 17:00.

units.title: Observing the Community
units.objective: Students can identify and verbally describe basic physical actions occurring in their community using the present continuous tense (-ing) with basic pronouns (he/she/I).

units.title: Community Service
units.objective: Students can demonstrate a functional understanding of 4 spatial prepositions and accurately answer simple "Where is...?" queries regarding localized objects.

units.title: Exploring the Community
units.objective: Students can communicate basic physiological states/feelings, ask/answer basic Yes/No questions regarding states, and describe the basic upkeep status of a public facility using basic adjectives.

units.title: Local Agricultural Specialties
units.objective: Students can name 8 localized agricultural crops, express basic eating preferences using "I like...", and correctly utilize proximity pointers (these vs. those).

units.title: Food, Fun, and Recreation
units.objective: Students can distinguish between common foods and beverages, communicate their likes, and properly accept or decline a culinary offering with appropriate courtesy phrases.

units.title: The Four Seasons of My Hometown
units.objective: Students can identify 6 types of weather and 4 seasons, characterize the relative climate temperature of each season, and articulate seasonal preferences.

units.title: Seasonal Feelings of My Hometown
units.objective: Students can integrate agricultural, seasonal, and locational elements to express affection for their hometown (Yunlin/Gukeng) and make simple invitations using "Let’s go to...".
target: Winter is the season for oranges.
Do you want some orange juice?

units.title: Welcome to Yunlin
units.sub: Yunlin Places & Days of the Week
units.objective: Students can identify and say the days of the week, ask and answer “What day is today?”, and use simple sentences to talk about activities in Yunlin.
target: What day is today? It’s Friday.
You can go to the night market in Douliu on Saturday.
You can visit the puppet show museum on Monday.
You can go to the park.

units.title: Three Meals in Yunlin
units.objective: Students can identify three meals of the day, name simple food in Yunlin, and talk about what they eat using “I eat ____.” and “You can eat _____.”
target: You can eat noodles in Yunlin.
You can eat snacks at the night market.
What would you like for breakfast?

units.title: Living in Yunlin
units.objective: Students can talk about family members, describe daily routines, ask and answer about daily schedules, and use simple present tense sentences about family life.
target: My grandfather is a farmer in ______.
What time does your grandfather go to work?
He goes to work at 7 AM.
I go to bed at 9 PM.

units.title: Travel Plan
units.objective: Students can talk about places in Yunlin, ask and answer where someone is going, use “I am going to _____” and “He/She is going to ____”, and identify famous landmarks in Yunlin.
target: There are many temples in Yunlin.
There is one theme park in Gukeng.
I am going to the theme park.
He/She is going to Chaotian Temple.

units.title: Marketing Yunlin / Yunlin Festivals
units.objective: Students can identify important festivals in Yunlin, ask and answer about festival dates, use months of the year to describe events, and promote Yunlin festivals using simple sentences.
target: When is the Gukeng Coffee Festival? It is in March.
When is the Sweet Potato Festival? It is in October.
When is the Lantern Festival? It is in February.
The Coffee Festival is in Gukeng.

units.title: Welcome to Taiwan
units.objective: Students can ask and answer about transportation in Taiwan, identify common transportation methods, give simple directions using “You can take…”, and describe locations using “Where is ____?” and “It is on ____ Road.”
target: How do I go to Taipei? You can take the HSR.

units.title: Famous Landmarks in Taiwan
units.objective: Students can identify famous places in Taiwan, ask and answer how to get to a place, give simple directions using “Go straight” and “Turn left/right,” and talk about their favorite places using simple sentences.
target: How can I get to Taipei 101?

units.title: Cultural Celebrations / Festivals in Taiwan
units.objective: Students can identify important festivals in Taiwan, ask and answer about festival dates, describe festivals using seasons and months, and talk about festival activities and traditional foods.
target: When is the Lantern Festival? It is in winter.
When is the Dragon Boat Festival? It is in summer.
People eat zongzi during the Dragon Boat Festival.
People eat mooncakes during the Mid-Autumn Festival.
People eat tangyuan during the Lantern Festival.
People have family reunions during Chinese New Year.

units.title: Shopping in Taiwan
units.objective: Students can ask and answer about prices, use “How much is/are ____?” in simple conversations, recognize and use basic money vocabulary in Taiwan, and describe prices using numbers in English.
target: How much is this bubble tea? It is 50 NT dollars.
How much is this beef noodle soup? It is ____ NT dollars.
How much are these pineapple cakes? They are ____ NT dollars.

units.title: Taiwan Industry
units.objective: Students can identify famous industries and products in Taiwan, describe what Taiwan is famous for, use simple sentences to talk about products and industries, and recognize products made in Taiwan.
target: Taiwan is famous for bubble tea.

units.title: Know The World
units.objective: Students will be able to recognize and locate countries on a world map, ask and answer questions about where people are from using target sentence patterns, and communicate basic information about countries and identities through role-play activities.

units.title: Tour Guide
units.objective: Students will be able to identify and draw representative features of different countries and use the sentence pattern “___ is famous for ___” to introduce a country’s specialties.
target: Taiwan is famous for xiao long bao.
The USA is famous for burgers.
The UK is famous for fish and fries.

units.title: We Are Not the Same: Food
units.objective: Students will be able to identify representative features of different places and countries and use the sentence pattern “___ is famous for ___” to introduce a country’s specialties.
target: What would you like to have/buy in Taiwan?
I would like to have sushi in Japan.
I would like to have beef noodles in Taiwan.
I would like to buy pineapple cakes in Taiwan.

units.title: We Are Not the Same: Clothing
units.objective: Students will be able to recognize and read vocabulary for countries and weather, match them with the correct clothing, and state appropriate clothing based on the weather and country using “People wear… in…”.
target: It's cold, what should I wear?
What do people wear in winter in Canada?
People wear boots and heavy coats.

units.title: World Attractions
units.objective: Students will be able to identify tourist attractions and use past tense question-and-answer patterns, and identify sentence structures and write them in the past tense.
target: Were you at Taipei 101 last weekend?
Last week, last year, last month

units.title: International Sporting Events
units.objective: Students can use the sentence pattern “What do you do in your free time?” and answer the question properly.
target: What do you do in your free time?
I play basketball in my free time.

units.title: Keeping Up with the Social Trends
units.objective: Students can use the sentence pattern “Who is your favorite singer/player/dancer …?” to describe their favorite people and jobs.

units.title: An Interesting World
units.objective: Students can identify different countries and say “Hello” in different languages, and practice speaking about countries, languages, and greetings in a meaningful context.
target: I'm from the USA. I speak English. This is the way I say hello, "Hello."
I'm from Japan. I speak Japanese. This is the way I say hello, "Konichiwa."
I'm from Korea. I speak Korean. This is the way I say hello, "An-nyeong-ha-se-yo."
I'm from Spain. I speak Spanish. This is the way I say hello, "Hola."

units.title: Let the Foreign Teachers Lead the Way
units.objective: Students can introduce/describe different places they have visited and describe their traveling experiences.
target: Did you sing / swim / dance / play soccer...?
Were you happy / tired / hungry / scared...?
Other questions (How many? How much? etc.)

units.title: Let’s Travel Around the World
units.objective: Students can identify different landmarks in different countries and describe their traveling plans.
target: Where do you want to go?
I want to go to Japan.
What would you like to see?
I would like to see Mt. Fuji.
